thread:
maria: Heads-up — noticed ~1.5k snapshot objects from last night's backup have no SSE headers (x-amz-server-side-encryption missing). Seen in prod bucket `redwood-db-snapshots`.
security-bot: [alert] object-store:missing-sse detected for prefix snapshots/2026-03-22/ — severity: high. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/90321
aj: Can you paste the sample object metadata? need to confirm if parts or entire object missing encryption metadata.
luca: quick note — we merged a change to the uploader library last night to simplify metadata injection. PR #4887 might be related: https://git.internal/redwood/uploader/pull/4887
maria: sample metadata:
```
Head: Content-Length: 104857600
x-amz-server-side-encryption: <absent>
x-amz-meta-origin: backup-service
``` 
maria: no SSE header. This is P1 until we confirm scope and whether keys were ever attached.
aj: running a CloudTrail query now for PutObject calls to that prefix between 2026-03-22T01:00Z and 2026-03-22T03:00Z. I'll share uploader principal list in a sec.
sam-oncall: Immediate mitigation: can we stop further unencrypted uploads? either revoke the uploader role or add a bucket policy requiring sse header.
luca: we can add an S3 bucket condition requiring "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption" header or restrict PutObject if missing. Quick patch:
```
{
  "Condition": {
    "StringNotEquals": {
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms"
    }
  }
}
```
luca: but be careful — if there are legitimate non-s3 backups we might block them. prefer toggling uploader svcacct until patch is out.
aj: CloudTrail shows uploader principal `svc-uploader@redwood` made 1.48k PutObject calls to that prefix between 02:10-02:35Z. The IAM call context shows no kms:GrantTokens were attached; likely metadata injection failed.
maria: any KMS grant issues? we recently shortened grant TTL for ephemeral uploads to 2m as an experiment.
aj: KMS logs look OK for other workflows. This is metadata not encryption issue — objects uploaded without SSE, so not wrapped at all. Re-encrypting could be done by copying the objects and applying SSE-KMS.
luca: plan for remediation:
  - block new uploads (sam-oncall)
  - run a dry-copy to re-encrypt a small sample with `aws s3 cp --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id alias/redwood-cmk` (luca)
  - build list of affected snapshot IDs and owners (aj)
  - coordinate restore validation and postmortem (maria)

luca: quick snippet I ran locally for a dry-run on one object:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-db-snapshots/snap-2026-03-22-0001 \
  s3://redwood-db-snapshots/snap-2026-03-22-0001 --metadata-directive REPLACE \
  --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:0123456789:key/abcd-efgh
```
aj: note: S3 copy will incur GET/PUT costs; for ~1.5k objects that's fine. We should also validate checksums after copy.
maria: erin (compliance) needs an audit timeline — include CloudTrail evidence, PRs, IAM changes, and exact object keys. aj please export the list and put in the incident doc.
sam-oncall: I'll open an incident page and revoke `svc-uploader` Write permission for the bucket (temporary). I'll also roll back the uploader change if we confirm it's the cause.
luca: I'll prepare a hotfix to reintroduce explicit SSE injection and add an integration test for metadata.
security-bot: Incident created: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-089 — severity P1, responders: @maria @aj @luca @sam-oncall
maria: After we patch, follow-up actions:
  - postmortem + runbook update to require bucket policy guard and uploader integration tests
  - add an alert for PutObject without sse header in prod
  - evaluate KMS grant TTL changes for uploader flow — too-short TTL might mask other issues

sam-oncall: assigned tasks in the incident. I'll also notify customer-success for the 4 customers who have restores in flight.
maria: thanks all. once aj uploads the CSV of affected objects I'll start the compliance timeline. :thumbsup:
aj: CSV uploaded to incident page + S3 manifest. starting validation run now.
luca: hotfix branch open, deploying canary to staging in 10m.
maria: we'll keep this thread for coordination. update incident doc with any blocking findings.
